page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include any local storage or GPU hardware. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The CPU achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1851.99 and a multi-core score of 15444.6, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 19492.46. Memory performance tests show a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 847.52 GB/sec, which drops to 99.57 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and a write bandwidth of 57.38 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the server processed 15.56 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved a static web serving throughput of 16.54 GB/sec. For lightweight machine learning tasks, the system processed 1266.34 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M parameter LLM, though performance drops to 32.12 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

The ecs.u1-c1m8.4xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of bundled local storage means users must rely on network-attached storage, which may be constrained by the 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This hardware profile is appropriate for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring substantial memory capacity without intensive local disk I/O.
